channel.title: Legitimate Peripheral Participation & Communities of Practice :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description: Working draft for faculty review. This page describes the general research basis for treating learning as participation in a practice, not just acquisition of content. For where this shows up concretely in the curriculum, see Chapter 3’s cornerstone projects — real, ongoing software systems students join and take on progressively larger roles in over the two-year core. What legitimate peripheral participation is Lave and Wenger’s central claim, developed from ethnographic studies of apprenticeship — Yucatec Mayan midwives, tailors in Vai and Gola communities, U.S. Navy quartermasters, meat cutters, and members of Alcoholics Anonymous — is that learning is not primarily an individual, cognitive process of absorbing decontextualized knowledge (Lave & Wenger, 1991). It is a process of increasing participation in a community of practice: a group of people bound together by a shared activity they are actually doing.
